feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader with clear domain focus, solid progression, and relevant technical breadth. It reads professionally and is rich in scope, but impact would improve with more quantified outcomes, tighter structure, and a few style/grammar fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline, summary, and experience consistently support a strong public-sector digital leadership brand.  
- Credibility and progression: long tenure at NACo with logical advancement from coordinator to director to consultant signals trust and growth.  
- Good evidence of scale: examples like a 10,000+ page migration, 3.5 million annual page views, and 50+ publishers add substance.

1. Top improvements  
- Add sharper results: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than outcomes; include measurable impact on engagement, efficiency, adoption, revenue, or campaign performance.  
- Simplify structure: there is overlap across Core Competencies, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT; consolidating these would reduce repetition and improve scanability.  
- Fix style consistency: “social, and multimedia” should remove the comma; “Ranked among the top public universities…” is weak/irrelevant for this level; maintain consistent punctuation in bullets and formatting for terms like “front-end/front end” and “organization-wide/organisation-wide” if targeting specific markets.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus. It reads well, but it is slightly dense and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and recent experience bullets.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten to one sharper value proposition and foreground the most relevant niche: enterprise digital modernization for public-sector organizations.
- Add scale or scope already supported elsewhere in the CV (for example, enterprise platforms, high-volume publishing, or cross-channel operations) without repeating detailed metrics.
- Simplify the list structure so it scans faster; “platforms, governance models and content operations” is strong, but the second sentence is too broad.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web platforms, governance models, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Leads digital strategy across web modernization, analytics, editorial systems, multimedia production, and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects; keep it brief here.
- The subtitle already signals leadership in digital platforms and communications systems, so avoid repeating too many capability labels in the intro.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-level leadership capabilities will make it feel more distinct and executive-level.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and trim wording for cleaner scanability.
- Replace “communications operations” with “communications leadership” to better reflect seniority.
- Consider this version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial systems • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • Multi-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- If space is tight, shorten “Multimedia production and livestream operations” to “Multimedia and livestream production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization” and “AI-enabled search and content experiences” repeat language already used in the header and recent projects.
- Several items also mirror Topline Skills almost exactly; consider making this section broader and more leadership-oriented.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it largely repeats achievements already covered in recent NACo roles. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make it feel more distinctive and higher impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and format each item consistently: project name + action + result.
- Replace generic verbs like “Built”/“Developed” with more specific leadership language: “Led,” “Launched,” “Architected,” “Produced.”
- Add measurable scope or outcome where possible (users, assets, campaign reach, event audience, content volume, timeline).
- Tighten wording for parallel structure, e.g. “AI Hybrid Search: Led design of an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level chat.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series closely overlap with the current consultant and NACo experience bullets.
- “Organization Anniversary Campaign” is the most distinct item; consider emphasizing projects not already described elsewhere.

Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email

items.title: Website

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with your prior NACo entries. Tighten it around what is new in this consulting engagement: advisory scope, technical delivery, and the AI/search initiative.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as 3–4 outcome-oriented bullets, e.g.:
- Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, content operations, and web governance for its public-facing communications ecosystem.
- Designed and implemented Drupal-based campaign and storytelling experiences, including modular microsites and downloadable member toolkits.
- Improved cross-channel workflows, analytics, and publishing systems to support more coordinated web, email, social, and multimedia communications.
- Led an AI-enabled site search initiative, defining retrieval strategy, structured content requirements, and user-facing discovery experience.
- Replace weak verbs like “consult,” “build and refine,” and “deliver” with “advise,” “designed,” “implemented,” “improved,” or “led.”
- Add metrics if available: number of sites/pages supported, workflow time saved, search accuracy gains, toolkit downloads, or engagement improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, workflows, analytics, and Drupal/web improvement” repeats the Director role; emphasize consultant-level advisory and AI/search work instead.
- Avoid restating broad channel ownership already covered in 2022–2024.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale signals; it should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and distinguish clearly from your earlier NACo roles. Right now, some bullets read as broad scope statements rather than achievement-driven results.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable impact where possible for channels/studio/analytics: subscriber growth, engagement rates, production volume, cost savings, reporting speed, or decision-making improvements.
- Tighten wording and reduce platform lists: e.g., “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast-quality studio, increasing capacity for advocacy programming, events, and recurring video content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance/publishing standards/workflows” overlaps with both the current consultant role and Associate Communications Director entry.
- Video expansion may partially duplicate the earlier “weekly advocacy video update” and “livestreams” bullets.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story and solid scope, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and distinct from the more strategic “Director of Digital Media” role above.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope statement: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social media, and video, supporting advocacy campaigns and organization-wide editorial operations.”
- Tighten bullets and emphasize ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Rephrase video bullet to show outcome: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring channel for policy communications.”
- Combine workflow/editorial bullets: “Built stronger editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy, and program teams, improving coordination and content consistency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthened editorial planning…” and “improved…publishing workflows” are repetitive; merge them.
- Avoid repeating broad channel oversight language already used in the 2022–2024 director role.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. Make it sharper, more senior, and more distinctive by emphasizing enterprise scope, governance, and mission-driven/public-sector context.

Suggested edit
- Replace broad phrases with higher-value wording: “Enterprise digital strategy” → “Enterprise digital strategy and transformation”; “Audience-focused content planning” → “Audience-centered content strategy and journey planning.”
- Tighten and elevate the list to 4 items max, e.g.:
- Enterprise digital strategy and transformation
- Editorial governance, workflow design, and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector, advocacy, and stakeholder messaging
- If space allows, add one differentiator tied to recent work: “Drupal-based platform modernization” or “AI-enabled content discovery strategy.”
- Keep terminology consistent with recent roles: use “governance,” “content operations,” and “platform modernization,” which are stronger than “content planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” duplicates “Multi-channel communication” in Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is already echoed in the header and multiple NACo entries.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value execution themes and the most relevant recent capabilities.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end web implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • SharePoint and Power Pages • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search and content discovery”
- Put Drupal and CMS modernization first, since recent NACo work makes these the strongest proof points.
- Replace “AI-enabled search experiences” with “AI-enabled search and content discovery” for clearer business value.
- Consider dropping one lower-priority platform if space is tight and tailoring by role; WordPress may be less important than Drupal/SharePoint/Power Pages for recent positioning.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills broader and save full tool inventory for the technical section.
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” also overlap with Core Competencies and Technical + IT.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list for the most recent leadership roles, but it reads as a generic inventory rather than a value-focused skills line. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing decision support/optimization will better match the impact shown in recent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, and Microsoft Clarity for KPI design, executive reporting, audience insights, and performance optimization.”
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “executive reporting” or “decision-ready reporting” for sharper wording.
- Consider changing “SEO and performance analysis” to “SEO, UX, and content performance analysis” if accurate; Clarity supports UX insight better than pure SEO.
- Order by strategic value, not software: “KPI design • Executive dashboards • Performance analysis • GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Data analytics & reporting” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating that exact phrase.
- Tool names also appear in recent work experience; keep this section concise and capability-oriented rather than repeating accomplishments.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong supporting skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and multiple NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and make the phrasing more senior and outcomes-oriented.

Suggested edit
- Replace generic terms with sharper, leadership-level phrasing: “Broadcast-quality video production,” “Live and hybrid event delivery,” “Studio build-out and operations,” “PTZ/multi-camera production systems.”
- Reorder by strategic value and recency: lead with live/hybrid event production and studio operations, then video production/editing, then PTZ systems.
- Consider a tighter rewrite: “Broadcast-quality video production & editing • Live, virtual and hybrid event production • Studio operations & in-house production workflows • PTZ and multi-camera livestream systems”
- If space allows elsewhere, connect to scale rather than tools alone (e.g., studio build-out, recurring advocacy programming, in-house capacity expansion).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Multimedia & live event production” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same wording.
- “Livestreaming” and “hybrid/virtual event production” are close; combine them to reduce redundancy.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills” and “Core Competencies.” This section should either be tighter or add light context that reinforces recent, relevant platform depth.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: Drupal (enterprise content architecture, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- If space allows, prioritize by strength/relevance: Drupal • SharePoint • WordPress • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- Consider dropping GitHub Pages unless it supports a specific recent project; it reads lighter than the other enterprise platforms.
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV; avoid repeating “CMS modernization” here since it already appears elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same tools plus stronger technical context.
- “Web & CMS administration” also appears in Core Competencies, so this entry should stay as a clean tool list rather than repeat capability language.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should be tighter, more implementation-focused, and emphasize current tools most relevant to recent Drupal/web systems work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as applied capabilities, not just languages: “Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag management integrations • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • Deployment automation (GitHub Actions)”
- Drop version numbers unless required: use “HTML, CSS” instead of “HTML5, CSS3” for a cleaner, more modern presentation.
- Consider replacing or qualifying broad items with stronger phrasing: “Google Tag Manager implementation” instead of just “Google Tag Manager.”
- If accurate, add scope/outcome context elsewhere on the CV rather than here, e.g., supported Drupal builds, analytics tagging, or deployment workflows for large public-facing sites.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Workflow automation” in Topline Skills may overlap with GitHub Actions; keep one at high level and one tool-specific.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems expertise. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already called out in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools**
- Tighten and group by function: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier | Jira • Asana • Trello • Basecamp | Slack • Microsoft Teams**
- If space allows, add light specialization instead of just listing tools: **Workflow automation, intake/tracking systems, editorial planning, cross-team collaboration**
- Prioritize tools most aligned to recent work; if Jira/Basecamp/Trello were less central recently, cut 1–2 to keep the list sharper.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and automation are already covered in **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; avoid repeating the same phrasing there.
- Slack/Teams are common workplace tools; keep them only if collaboration platforms are genuinely part of your systems-building story.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful category, but it reads as a bare software list and misses the scale/strategic email work shown in recent NACo roles. Strengthen it by signaling CRM/email automation capability without repeating newsletter details already covered in experience.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing, CRM & Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, make it more capability-led: **Email marketing automation • CRM-based audience journeys • Newsletter and member engagement platforms (Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys, Higher Logic, Mailchimp)**
- Keep only platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; order by strongest/recentest platform first.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding outcomes like “tens of thousands reached” here; that impact is already covered in Work Experience.
- “Engagement Systems” overlaps slightly with “Automation & Workflow Systems”; keep this item focused on email/CRM platforms only.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills” and misses a chance to show level of capability. Tighten it into a sharper technical stack entry and emphasize analysis/optimization rather than repeating broad terms.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics & Optimization Stack**
- Replace with: **GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • SEO analysis • A/B testing • KPI/dashboard reporting**
- Prefer more specific phrasing: change **SEO** to **SEO analysis** and **Dashboarding** to **KPI/dashboard reporting** to signal applied business use.
- If space allows elsewhere, add one proof point tied to recent work, e.g. “supported reporting for a 10,000+ page Drupal migration and 3.5M annual page views” rather than adding more tools here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates **Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider keeping the detailed tool list here and shortening/removing the topline version.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already validated in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid repeating extra analytics claims without outcomes.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful “first in-house digital team” context, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo entries on workflows, weekly video updates, and cross-channel operations. Make it more execution-focused and specific to this earlier stage.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize foundational build work and production ownership: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Add clearer scope/results if available: website refresh size, livestream/event volume, video cadence, audience reach, or process improvements.
- Tighten the second sentence to concrete contributions: “Supported a major website refresh, produced livestreams and weekly video updates, and helped formalize day-to-day publishing workflows.”
- Replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with stronger management phrasing if accurate: “mentored” or “supervised” a digital media associate.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” repeats the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this item as the launch/early production phase.
- “Strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia” overlaps with later operations-focused bullets; keep this version lighter and more foundational.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows the start of your multimedia/digital trajectory, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize the podcast launch and any concrete research/program outputs.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the most distinctive achievement: “Coordinated innovation and policy research projects for NACo programs; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Replace vague phrases like “supporting organizational programs and policy work” and “contributed to digital content production” with specific deliverables: reports, briefs, web features, multimedia series, stakeholder interviews, etc.
- If possible, add scale or outcomes: number of episodes launched, audiences reached, projects supported, or teams/programs served.
- Keep this entry shorter than later NACo roles since those better demonstrate senior digital leadership.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; avoid repeating generic multimedia language.
- Since later entries cover video and digital operations in depth, use this role to highlight research/policy coordination + first podcast launch.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with stronger, higher-level multimedia claims elsewhere. Make it more tool-focused and concise, with only the production capabilities not already covered in Topline Skills/Core Competencies.

Suggested edit:
